renderMechanic.depthCap: DEFAULT_CANVAS_MAX_DEPTH = 4. Focal product is depth 0; BFS stops expanding a node once depth>=4, so children added below an existing depth-4 node DO NOT RENDER. Every proposed node must land at depth<=4 to count toward the rendered floor.
renderMechanic.scoping: loadActiveGraphData(root) -> scopeGraphToReachableNodes (forward BFS over ALL relations, no depth cap) decides the TOTAL node set; orgs reachable only via a supplier edge to an UNWIRED component are excluded from total until that component is wired with `requires`.

_meta.structuralDiagnosis: Deficit is NOT shallowness (SpaceX spine already reaches depth 6, deeper than flagship's 4). It is (a) NARROW TOP: tree splits at layer-1 into 2 vehicle technical_routes (Falcon9 / Starship) + 2 small modules = 4 first-layer children, vs flagship's 7 parallel SUBSYSTEM modules; (b) ORPHANED EVIDENCED NODES: ~19 already-authored, ok_exact-cited component nodes (TVC actuators, valves, igniters, bearings, AM machines, radhard FPGA, IMU/GNSS, star tracker, connectors, FTS ordnance, PICA/ceramic tiles, carbon fiber) attach ONLY via `part_of` (wrong relation) + supplier edges (stripped), so they are invisible; (c) ENGINE INTERNALS are DEPTH-BLOCKED: Falcon9 booster->engine cluster and Starship vehicle->booster->engine sit at d3-d5, so adding engine sub-components hits the depth-4 wall. The flagship gets width by enumerating, per subsystem module at d1, every key EQUIPMENT + PROCESS + input MATERIAL as sibling d2 children. SpaceX instead chains engineering_method know-how nodes downward. The deepening must add real sibling component/material/process children at the SHALLOW frontiers (avionics d2, fairing d2, second stage d2, ground d2, structures/legs/grid-fin/COPV d3) where depth budget (4-depth) >= 1.
